posts.text:
On November 12, 1918 — one day after the armistice — one of Europe's great empires simply stopped existing.

Half a dozen new states appeared on the map overnight.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Austria-Hungary wasn't one nation — it was 11+ ethnic groups held together by the Habsburg crown. When the war effort collapsed, so did the glue. The empire didn't just lose a war and shrink; it came apart.

2/ Some of the new states on this map never made it past 1919: the West Ukrainian People's Republic, the Banat Republic, even tiny peasant republics like Tarnobrzeg and Komańcza — on the map for months, gone within a year.
3/ German-speaking Austria voted to join Germany, but the peace treaties that followed explicitly banned that merger (Anschluss) — a ban Hitler would break in 1938.

4/ Czechoslovakia and the new Yugoslavia (State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs) were the empire's biggest winners, absorbing German Bohemia, Sudetenland and the South Slav lands into single states — unions that would themselves fracture decades later.
5/ Hungary lost roughly two-thirds of its pre-war territory in the process — the "Trianon trauma" still central to Hungarian politics today.

6/ One empire, a dozen successor states, and border lines still visible on the map of Central Europe.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
